title: Poisson Decision Limits for Private ATT Intervals with Two Covariate Strata and Few Treated
banked_reason: Field floor not met: D0.5.G achieved incremental with paper_score_ceiling 6.2 below 7.4; canonical LP evaluability repair merged; remaining scope is two binary strata and no tight moderate-parameter continuum value.
gap_reasons: The proved result is an exact asymptotic reduction for a highly specialized two-stratum, binary-outcome triangular array with treatment probabilities fixed exactly at lambda_x/n and connected-interval loss.

It does not analytically determine the Poisson decision value or deliver a tight numerical continuum enclosure; the only computed coarse grid is explicitly unusable for that purpose, so the advertised calibration value remains an implicit infinite-game quantity.
The strict-gap theorem is witnessed at lambda_min=400 and epsilon=0.0001 and therefore does not establish a practically representative small-count privacy penalty.
paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived an all-mechanism rare-ATT Poisson frontier, a total Borel selector at unchanged privacy and coverage budgets, an explicit one-third convergence rate, a strict private/nonprivate gap, and a canonical rationally checkable finite-LP enclosure. The math review passed and a bounded D0 repair resolved the decision reviewer's LP-evaluability finding; the general referee still graded the delivered two-stratum result incremental below the field floor. A field-tier successor would need a new fixed-support generalization and a tight value enclosure at a representative parameter tuple.
tldr: With two binary covariate strata and \(O(1)\) treated records, private ATT uncertainty has a non-Gaussian decision limit. The finite-sample all-mechanism minimax connected-interval length converges, at unchanged \((\varepsilon,\delta,\alpha)\), to the known-abundant-nuisance four-mark Poisson count-graph value. The attaining selector uses a total Borel pure-private nuisance pilot and canonical graph-private finite-program rules. The certificate program is uniquely generated from the public tuple, cap, and three meshes: it has endpoint-inclusive uniform grids, explicit clipped-Poisson coefficients, every add-delete-substitute edge, and complete output-subset approximate-privacy rows. Directed dyadic coefficient enclosures, exact rational primal and residual-corrected dual checks, and common-output defect repair make its two-sided bounds reproducible without enlarging privacy or miscoverage. The audited schedule retains \(|L_n-L_{\mathrm{Pois}}|=O((\log n/n)^{1/3})\), and the separate honest nonprivate benchmark retains the strict private-versus-nonprivate gap on an explicit open region. The independently computed coarse \(16\)-state instance remains non-tight and is not a continuum calibration.
gap: Published private ATT and WATE procedures use fixed positivity and growing effective counts, while PrivATE and the model-agnostic procedures of Lebeda, Even, Bellet, and Josse target the ATE through regular Gaussian utility or interval arguments under fixed overlap. Exact private binomial intervals live on a one-dimensional count chain. None determines the all-mechanism decision value when zero treated records retain positive probability and a full-record treatment flip induces add, delete, and substitute moves among four marks.
fill: The eventual-domain graph simulation, total Borel private abundant-nuisance selector with deterministic zero-denominator defaults, continuum LP enclosure, separate honest nonprivate Poisson benchmark, and robust strict-gap witness jointly identify, attain, certify, and interpret the rare-ATT frontier without importing the regular-count assumptions or favored mechanisms of the comparator procedures.
